subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep the current per-job `toolsAllow` model with targeted delivery safeguards?
rationale: This adds or changes a security-sensitive config surface, and repository policy requires maintainer intent for new config/default behavior and tool-access boundaries.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce a first-class cron tool-policy layer with explicit precedence against existing tool policies and per-job `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Make cron runs reuse `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface but coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Do not add global cron policy; instead rely on `payload.toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery-mode safeguards.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a first-class cron tool-policy layer with explicit precedence against existing tool policies and per-job `toolsAllow`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has recent history on cron/session policy surfaces and already provided the earlier maintainer-facing review on this issue.
